claim: On a curated 2024 ICPC/CCPC competitive-programming benchmark judged via online judge, only 5 of 80 (6.25%) problems were fully accepted with a basic prompt, evidencing the strict all-or-nothing acceptance criterion of competitive-programming grading.
stance_target: DPRC's claim that competitive code correctness is all-or-nothing, with ~0% partial-pass at baseline
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-R1, 80 problems from 9 regional ICPC/CCPC 2024 contests, basic prompting
quoted_support: Experimental results show that only 5 out of 80 problems are fully accepted when using basic prompts.

claim: Competitive-programming solution failures were categorized into a fine-grained error taxonomy (general: design, boundary, condition, data-type, syntax, I/O errors; specialized: math, greedy, graph-theory errors) rather than being graded by partial per-test credit.
stance_target: characterization of failure modes in competitive code without a native partial-credit signal
quoted_support: Error taxonomy includes general errors (such as design, boundary, condition, data type, syntax, and input/output errors) and specialized errors (such as those in mathematical problems, greedy algorithms, and graph theories)
